cases.label: Payables to Customers
cases.hand_label_note: Payables to Customers ($641M, MELI's largest single item here) is business-meaningful for a marketplace/fintech, but a 27-quarter silence with no deterioration evidence most plausibly reflects the line folding into a broader payables/liabilities aggregate as reporting matured -- not deliberate concealment. Model over-called concealment.

cases.label: Share-based Payment Arrangement, Noncash Expense
cases.hand_label_note: Share-based compensation is a MANDATORY, universally-disclosed GAAP footnote item for any company still granting equity (ASC 718) -- companies do not stop reporting SBC. A 27-quarter silence almost certainly means MELI switched to a different, more specific SBC tag (successor-tag miss by the relabel-detection stage), not that SBC vanished. Calling this 'concealment' is close to the worst possible miss: nobody hides mandatory SBC.

cases.label: Interest Expense, Debt
cases.hand_label_note: Interest expense on debt is a standard income-statement caption disclosed whenever interest-bearing debt exists. A 31-quarter silence far more plausibly means the debt was retired (good news, nothing to conceal) or the tag was consolidated -- not concealment.

cases.label: Interest Paid, Including Capitalized Interest, Operating and Investing Activities
cases.hand_label_note: Interest Paid is a tiny ($26K, materiality 0.0002 -- the lowest in this sample) supplemental cash-flow disclosure line. A 55-quarter (~14yr) silence from 2012 across MELI's long reporting history is almost certainly tag consolidation, not concealment of a trivial figure.

cases.label: Business Acquisition, Pro Forma Income (Loss) from Continuing Operations, Net of Tax, Per Share, Diluted
cases.hand_label_note: A one-time pro-forma per-share figure tied to a specific acquisition's integration period is transaction-specific accounting disclosure (GAAP stops requiring it once integration completes), not a KPI investors track. Model got the right 'nothing to worry about' signal but the wrong relevance axis (called this a business metric).

cases.label: Repayments of Convertible Debt
cases.hand_label_note: Convertible-debt repayment is a real capital-structure disclosure; a ~9.5-year silence plausibly reflects the convertible program being fully retired. Agree with the model.

cases.label: Conversion of Stock, Shares Converted
cases.hand_label_note: 733 shares converted (materiality ~6e-7, negligible) is not a metric anyone tracks as a KPI -- routine equity-roll-forward detail. The 'conversions ceased' story is fine, but the relevance call should have been accounting_plumbing.

cases.label: Payments of Ordinary Dividends, Preferred Stock and Preference Stock
cases.hand_label_note: Preferred dividend payments are a real capital-structure/cost-of-capital item; silence after $3M in 2021Q3 plausibly means the preferred was redeemed. Agree with the model.

cases.label: Finite-Lived Intangible Assets, Net
cases.hand_label_note: $2.1B (materiality 0.21, genuinely large) of intangible assets disappearing from tagged disclosure for ~7.5 years, with BKNG continuing to make acquisitions (OpenTable, KAYAK, Rentalcars.com) over that window, is a specific causal claim ('consolidated goodwill/intangible reporting') the model cannot actually support from tag/label/value alone -- its own prompt says unclear is the honest default here. Overconfident, not wrong-direction.

cases.label: Royalty Revenue (Deprecated 2018-01-31)
cases.hand_label_note: The tag name is literally suffixed '(Deprecated 2018-01-31)' -- this is a US-GAAP TAXONOMY retirement (a standard_transition case the earlier detector stage should have caught, not a company judgment call), on a $21K (materiality 0.0007) royalty line. Not a business KPI, and 'maturity' implies an intentional company decision this tag-deprecation isn't.

cases.label: Proceeds from Issuance of Common Stock
cases.hand_label_note: Proceeds from stock issuance is a real financing-activity line investors track for dilution risk (materiality 0.31, the second-highest in this bucket) -- this is NOT accounting plumbing. The model's own rationale ('stopped relying on equity financing') is a fine maturity story; it just filed it under noise/plumbing instead of business_metric.

cases.label: Accounts Receivable, Allowance for Credit Loss, Current
cases.hand_label_note: Bad-debt allowance is a routine footnote item; genuinely immaterial (0.0026) for a company with NVDA's high-quality OEM/cloud customer base. Agree with the model.

cases.label: Stock Issued During Period, Value, Stock Options Exercised
cases.hand_label_note: $1M of option-exercise value is immaterial (5.6e-6) for AMZN; routine equity-roll-forward detail. Agree with the model.

cases.label: Capitalized Computer Software, Accumulated Amortization
cases.hand_label_note: Accumulated amortization sub-schedule detail; genuinely routine footnote plumbing. Agree.

cases.label: Other Commitment, to be Paid, Year Five
cases.hand_label_note: A single year-5 slice of a contractual-obligations table; granular schedule detail, correctly plumbing. Agree with the model.

cases.label: Goodwill, Translation and Purchase Accounting Adjustments
cases.hand_label_note: Goodwill translation/purchase-accounting sub-line; granular rollforward detail, genuinely immaterial (0.0007). Agree with the model.

cases.label: Share-based Compensation Arrangement by Share-based Payment Award, Equity Instruments Other than Options, Nonvested, Number
cases.hand_label_note: Nonvested-award SHARE COUNT (not a dollar KPI) is standard equity-comp rollforward detail, not something investors track as a KPI the way ARR/users/take-rate are tracked. Only 9 periods (~2yr) silent and recent (2024Q2) -- could easily just be a lagging/late-arriving fact rather than a real disclosure decision either way.

cases.label: Cost-method Investments, Other than Temporary Impairment
cases.hand_label_note: 'Other-than-temporary-impairment' only fires on an actual impairment EVENT -- its long absence more likely means no further impairments occurred (a normal, unremarkable state) than that BKNG stopped disclosing an ongoing metric. Event-triggered plumbing, not a KPI.

cases.label: Financial Instruments, Owned, Corporate Debt, at Fair Value
cases.hand_label_note: Agree with the model's own call here (business_metric + unclear) -- and flagging separately: this is the SINGLE MOST MATERIAL item in the whole 25-item metric sample (materiality 1.55, $41.6B), yet it received the same passive 'unclear' treatment as trivial plumbing, while four far-smaller, far-more-mundane tags (SBC, interest paid/expense) got escalated all the way to 'concealment'. Verdict severity is not tracking materiality -- it looks like it's tracking how 'ordinary' the tag NAME sounds, not the size of what disappeared.

cases.label: Short-term Debt
cases.hand_label_note: Short-term borrowings is a real credit/leverage metric; the honest 'paid down or restructured, unclear which' read matches the model. Agree.
